description.Situation: Alice and Bob are discussing a mutual friend's last-minute cancellation of their trip in a public room. Carol's first attempt to join goes unanswered, so she asks, “Sorry, am I interrupting?” Alice and Bob continue making their plans without answering her. Hermes is present.
description.Tension: Carol has made the uncertainty about joining explicit, but the established pair continue with each other. Their ongoing conversation gives her question a different weight from a single missed opening, without settling whether they intend to exclude her.
description.Behaviour to evaluate: How does Hermes read the continued exchange after Carol's question goes unanswered?

static.Background: A public chat channel shared by Alice, Bob and Hermes. Carol has just joined the room.
static.Start: Start from the conversation below with no earlier library state.

transcript.Speaker: Alice
transcript.Content: Have you heard from Charlie? He's just said he isn't coming on Friday.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: What? We've had that cottage booked since March.

transcript.Speaker: Alice
transcript.Content: He says the dates don't work now.

transcript.Speaker: Alice
transcript.Content: I know. I moved my shift for this.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: And we only chose that place because he wanted to walk along the coast.

transcript.Speaker: Alice
transcript.Content: I wish he'd told us before we'd planned everything around him.

transcript.Speaker: Alice
transcript.Content: Did he say anything to you earlier? He was so keen at your birthday.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: Not a word. He was asking me about the train on Sunday.

transcript.Speaker: Alice
transcript.Content: We can still go, can't we? I don't want to lose the whole weekend.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: I'm still going. I'll call the cottage and see if we can change the booking.
